headline: Big 5 Construct Saudi 2026 by the numbers
deck: The figures that describe the show and the market it opened into, from 1,000 exhibitors and 35,000 expected visitors to 233 products with local content deadlines and 13,660 licensed factories.
excerpt: Big 5 Construct Saudi ran from 30 August to 2 September at Riyadh Front under Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources patronage. This is the reference set of figures: the show's scale and structure, the three Impact Trail awards, the corporate announcements, and the policy numbers on local content, the building code, industrial licensing and facilities management that give the edition its forward reading.
content:
Big 5 Construct Saudi 2026 ran from 30 August to 2 September at the Riyadh Front Exhibition & Conference Center at ROSHN Front, next to King Khalid International Airport, under the patronage of the Ministry of Industry and Mineral Resources, with the halls open from 4pm to 10pm each day, according to the organiser. It was opened by Eng Fawaz bin Badr Al Shora, Deputy Minister of Industry and Mineral Resources for Industrial Services and Compliance, as BrentDesk reported. More than 1,000 exhibitors from over 50 countries took stands, and the organiser's stated expectation was more than 35,000 trade visitors. This is the reference set of figures for the edition.

The structure was five shows in one building. The main Big 5 halls covered general construction and building materials. Heavy Saudi Arabia took earthmoving equipment, cranes and specialist trucks onto an outdoor site of more than 20,000 square metres with live demonstrations. Totally Concrete Saudi Arabia covered concrete production, materials and precast, HVACR Saudi Arabia covered cooling, ventilation and refrigeration, and Saudi FM & Clean covered facilities management, cleaning, hygiene and waste. The conference programme ran across nine topic areas, from codes and standards to artificial intelligence, concrete, modular construction and HVACR, with speaking organisations including the Saudi Building Code Center, ROSHN Group, SEVEN, Misk City, Saudi Binladin Group, Kabbani Construction Group, Al Kholi Group, Modern Building Leaders and Dussman Ajlan & Bros, and two named speakers, Christopher Seymour of Mace Consult and Shonagh Kinnaird of Misk City.

The formal announcements were the three Big 5 Impact Trail awards. Prime Middle East Trading Company, trading as PRIMECO, won sustainability innovation for its work with Honeywell's Solstice low-global-warming-potential refrigerants. Masdar won best circular economy solution for Kronospan carbon-negative wood-based panels and engineered boards. Al-Futtaim Engineering Company won operational sustainability for an integrated facilities management solution. The programme also spotlighted three companies: Galaxy Technology, with Albion Valves and published carbon data across its cast-iron range, Star Factory in spray polyurethane foam roofing and waterproofing, and Keller in ground improvement and foundations.

The corporate record has four lines. One product debut: Kiwi Information Technology Co. Ltd. launched Philips Home Access Solutions in the Kingdom and expanded its Saudi channel partnerships, according to the company. One service-line launch: Al-Futtaim Contracting combined Al-Futtaim Facilities Management with the fire and life safety division of Al-Futtaim Engineering to launch integrated operations in Saudi Arabia. One certification partnership: Eurovent Certita Certification exhibited with Eurovent Middle East, promoting a Desert Certification option that tests at 35C and 46C, requires demonstrated operability at 52C and publishes a part-load Desert Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio for the six GCC markets. And zero headline construction contract awards, which is normal for a sourcing exhibition.

Three policy figures give the edition its forward reading. The Local Content and Government Procurement Authority has tied benefit from the mandatory list of national products to a minimum local content percentage recorded in an enterprise-level Local Content Certificate, covering 233 products from 1 August this year and adding split air conditioners, water pumps, water valves and copper wires from 1 August 2027, the Saudi Press Agency reported. The 2024 Saudi Building Code has been mandatory since 30 June 2025 after a 180-day transition, the Saudi Building Code Center was constituted as a standalone body under the Ministry of Municipalities and Housing by Council of Ministers decision in March 2025, and an occupancy certificate is now a prerequisite for full electrical activation, according to Chambers.

The industrial base the patronage points at is measurable. There were 13,660 industrial facilities active in the Kingdom at the end of April 2026, up more than 11 per cent year on year, with 322 new industrial licences issued in April carrying investment above SAR 12.33 billion, Jawlah reported.

So is the demand. Saudi construction output is forecast to grow 6.2 per cent in 2026 to about SAR 232.14 billion. Contract awards tracked by the Saudi Contractors Authority reached their 2026 high in May at more than SR 30.03 billion across 18 projects, 10 of them infrastructure worth more than SR 25 billion, and June brought the year's highest count, 25 awards worth more than SR 29.5 billion, with building and construction taking 14 projects and 56 per cent of the value. On the operating side, Mordor Intelligence puts outsourced facilities management at close to 60 per cent of the Saudi market, growing around 8 per cent a year.

The show returns to Riyadh in 2027. The figures to check then are the ones this list leaves open: how many localisation intentions have become licensed plants, and whether the award categories have a Saudi manufacturer among their winners. What defined the edition and the corporate record are the companion pieces.
